conversations.value: Where does Sunday get its name?

Sunday is a modern echo of the pantheon: Latin diēs Sōlis — the day of Sōl, the Roman sun god (Greek Hēlios). The name lives in the calendar (or the sky, or the dictionary) exactly because the god’s name carried power for the people who carried the word — the restoration (the) is the same name with its marks recovered.

Does the word "panic" really come from a god's name?

It does — Pan haunts lonely places, and the terror that falls on travelers there — the pounding heart, the need to run — the Greeks called panikón deima, Pan-fear. The god who startles flocks gave his name to the feeling. (Greek panikós (of Pan) → French panique → English panic). An ordinary English word carrying a divine name two or three thousand years deep: the myth did not end; it went lexical. The temple: /pan/.

It does — The nymph Ēkhō, cursed (or loved) into having no voice of her own, may only answer with the last words she hears. Every canyon that throws your voice back is speaking her name. (). An ordinary English word carrying a divine name two or three thousand years deep: the myth did not end; it went lexical. The temple: /echo/.
